title: Brazil awards 228 MW grid capacity to three data center projects
source_used: W.Media (9 Oct 2026, from a translated ONS press release) and ET Datacenters (10 Oct 2026)
key_facts: Brazil's National Electric System Operator (ONS) awarded 228 MW of grid capacity to three data center projects under the 1st 2026 Access Season of the National Transmission System Access Policy (PNAST).
The capacity was the remaining grid capacity at four connection points in São Paulo state, awarded in a competitive process; seven projects took part with 451 MW of qualified demand.

All 228 MW went to Pahlavan One, Pahlavan Three (both on CloudHQ's GRU campus) and Digital DC Brasil (under NextStream, created by investment firm Actis), which will expand NextStream's Tamboré campus.

367 projects registered in the first Access Season, requesting more than 20 GW at 64 substation connection points; ONS assessed over 43 GW of requests including the transitional phase, about 30.7 GW viable or qualified.
From 2027 ONS will run two Access Seasons a year.
quote_evidence: On Tuesday, all 228 MW of the capacity was awarded to Pahlavan One, Pahlavan Three, and Digital DC Brasil.
As many as 367 projects registered in the 1st Access Season, requesting more than 20 GW of connections at 64 substation connection points across Brazil’s national grid.
why_it_matters_hint: Grid access for data centers in Brazil is now decided in competitive rounds and demand far exceeds supply.
notes: W.Media (9 Oct) is the first outlet found and cites a translated ONS press release; ET Datacenters (10 Oct) repeats it.
